parsed.explanation: Thin, dated dossier, so I extrapolate from structural signals. Against the visitor: sections 153-155 criminalise male same-sex conduct (up to 14 years), with no enforcement reported in 2015 and no later prosecutions found; there is no statutory protection for gender identity outside employment, and that employment law names sexual orientation but not gender identity; the constitutional non-discrimination guarantee omits both; the 2016 source confirms the statute was still on the books. For the visitor: the 2015 no-violence observation is a decade old and cannot be treated as current; there is no documented trans-specific targeting, but also no post-2015 climate data. Entry screening, document rules, facility and custody rules, and care access are unsourced, so they are open questions, not findings. Mitigating: a traditional gender role is documented regionally, which may reduce reading of presentation as deviant, though the sources describe cultural roles, not legal status. No recourse for trans people is documented. Resolving the thin record toward its structural risk puts this in the elevated band.
